To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose an integrated approach for the design of critical software systems, which is based on a combination of behavioural software designs with dependability models.

the proposed approach allows to: 1) assess if a software design meets a given dependability requirement (in terms of a dependability degree); 2) assess if a given dependability degree is met if we integrate in a software design a specific FT technique; and 3) assess if a FT technique can be integrated into a software design to meet a specific dependability requirement.
the combination of UML and Petri nets can be used to model software designs equipped with specification about the use of fault tolerant techniques.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to integrate FT techniques in the design of critical systems.
a methodology to assist the software engineers to develop dependable systems, and to assess the impact of a given fault-tolerant technique in a given software design.
the development of a tool that supports software engineers in the early stages of software design.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this research is about the integration of fault-tolerant models in software behavioural design models.

we have proposed a formal model to assist the software designer to evaluate the adequacy of a given dependability requirement for a given software system, in terms of a set of fault-tolerant design patterns.
the combination of the proposed techniques and tools would allow the software engineer to assess the adequacy of a dependability technique for a given software architecture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are developing a methodology for the integration of dependability techniques into software designs.
we propose a formal model to integrate FT techniques into a software behavioural design.
we are working on a tool to help software engineers to assess if a given fault-tolerant technique is adequate for the system under design.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to combine both software behavioural designs and fault-tolerant models to assess the adequacy of a technique to a software design.
we can help software engineers to make decisions regarding the use of fault-tolerant software techniques, i.e., to know if a given technique is adequate for the software design at hand.
we will provide an early and automatic way to assess if a software design can be enhanced with a given FT technique to meet a given dependability requirement.
